target.title: fix(cp): prefer secluded rsync args for resolved SSH copies
target.body:
## Problem

The `Connector E2E Smokes / ssh-localhost` job failed on main ([run 29678510518](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/actions/runs/29678510518/job/88170257394)) at `cp download over resolved SSH`:

```
rsync: [sender] link_stat "/tmp/crabbox-ssh-localhost-KjHarK/workroot/cp remote[1].txtU" failed: No such file or directory (2)
rsync error: some files/attrs were not transferred (see previous errors) (code 23)
```

Note the phantom trailing `U` (hex-verified against the raw job log: a literal 0x55 byte). The same code passed at 06:40 and on the PR branch runs — the failure is intermittent, and PR #1160 (the failing merge) touched nothing SSH/cp-related.

## Root cause: upstream rsync `safe_arg()` uninitialized byte

`rsyncRemoteCopyPath()` escapes literal wildcards for the remote shell (`cp remote[1].txt` → `cp remote\[1].txt`), which is rsync's documented convention. But rsync's client-side `safe_arg()` (options.c) has a count/write mismatch for exactly this input:

- the **counting** pass counts every backslash as needing an escape (`\` is in `SHELL_CHARS`), sizing the buffer with `extras` bytes;
- the **writing** pass intentionally does *not* double a backslash that precedes a wildcard in a filename arg (`if (!is_filename_arg || !strchr(WILD_CHARS, f[1]))`);
- termination then uses the counted length: `ret[len1+len2+extras] = '\0'` — **one byte past the written content**, leaving one uninitialized heap byte inside the arg handed to the remote shell.

Instrumenting `safe_arg()` in a pinned rsync 3.4.4 build shows it directly (`strlen(ret)=135`, `expected=136` for the smoke's path; on an ubuntu:24.04 run the gap byte surfaced as `0x5c`). Whenever the gap byte is non-zero, the remote shell receives `…txt<garbage>` — on the failing runner it was `0x55` (`U`).

Why it appeared now: rsync 3.4.0–3.4.3 zeroed all allocations, masking the gap byte; **3.4.4 reverted that zeroing** (`alloc: revert "zero all new memory"`, upstream #959), and CI pins 3.4.4. Older 3.2.x/3.3.x are exposed the same way, so user machines can hit this too — it is not CI-only. Whether a given run fails depends purely on heap history, hence the flakiness.

## Fix

Route around the entire class of shell-transported-arg bugs: probe the remote rsync for secluded-args support (`rsync --protect-args --version` — the same probe WSL2 targets already hard-require) and pass `--secluded-args` whenever the remote supports it. Remote paths then travel over the rsync protocol stream and never appear on the remote shell command line, so `safe_arg()`'s escaping path is never taken (it early-returns the arg untouched). Remotes without secluded support — notably macOS **openrsync**, which rejects `-s` outright — keep the existing `--no-secluded-args` shell-transported behavior unchanged.

- `--secluded-args` sources keep the literal-wildcard escaping (server-side globbing honors backslash escapes), matching the existing WSL2 behavior; destinations use the existing `rsyncSecludedRemoteDestinationPath()` handling.
- The hostile `RSYNC_OLD_ARGS=1 RSYNC_PROTECT_ARGS=1` env the smoke sets remains defeated by explicit flags.

## Verification

- Unit tests: secluded flag selection, operand escaping in both modes, probe-failure fallback to `--no-secluded-args`, probe-success preference for `--secluded-args`. Full `go test ./internal/cli/` passes.
- End-to-end in an ubuntu:24.04 container mirroring CI (pinned rsync 3.4.4 client on PATH, distro rsync 3.2.7 as the sshd-side default): with client-side rsync malloc poisoned to `0x55` via `LD_PRELOAD`, the **old binary reproduces the smoke failure deterministically** (the upload leg even creates `cp remote[1].txt<garbage>` so the script's `chmod` fails), and the **fixed binary passes the full smoke** (`classification=live_ssh_localhost_smoke_passed … cp=roundtrip`) under the same poisoning.
- Cross-version copies validated by hand for 3.4.4→3.4.4 and 3.4.4→3.2.7, both directions, bracket + space filenames, with `--secluded-args`.

Worth reporting upstream to rsync as well; happy to file that separately.
